hook: A crack in the ground, spraying lava into rivers that ran to the sea.
narration: Lava shot out of a crack in the ground, feeding rivers of molten rock.
This was the Fissure 20 complex on Kilauea, Hawaii, on May 21, 2018.
A fissure eruption opens a long crack instead of one vent, so lava fountains up along a whole line.
The lava split into channels, joined again near the coast, then split once more.
outcome: The channels carried the lava all the way to the ocean.
title: Lava fountains roar out of Kilauea
question_comment: Would you fly over an eruption like this?

extra_sources.excerpt: The video concludes with a view of the bifurcating lava channels that merge closer to the coast (and split again before ocean entry).

description:
A U.S. Geological Survey overflight of the Fissure 20 complex on Kilauea, Hawaii, on May 21, 2018, showed fissure fountains feeding lava channels that ran to the ocean.
